sentences.en: Hi there, Shankar here.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是香卡。

sentences.en: We're in the middle of our summer series called U 2.0.
sentences.zh: 我们正在进行名为“U 2.0”的夏季系列节目。

sentences.en: This week's episode comes from our early days of Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周的节目精选自我们《隐藏大脑》早期的内容。

sentences.en: It looks at who comes up with great ideas and what we can do to have more of them.
sentences.zh: 它探讨了伟大点子源自何人，以及我们如何能想出更多点子。

sentences.en: Adam Grant was teaching his first class at the Wharton Business School
sentences.zh: 亚当·格兰特正在沃顿商学院讲授他的第一堂课

sentences.en: when a student came up to him with an interesting proposition.
sentences.zh: 当时一个学生带着一个有趣的提议找到了他。

sentences.en: He says, I've got this big idea.
sentences.zh: 他说，我有一个宏大的想法。

sentences.en: Three friends and I are going to start an online business
sentences.zh: 我和三个朋友打算创办一家在线企业

sentences.en: and we're going to disrupt an industry.
sentences.zh: 我们要颠覆整个行业。

sentences.en: Do you want to invest?
sentences.zh: 你想投资吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But from what Adam could see, this group of friends wasn't doing so well
sentences.zh: 但以亚当当时的观察，这群朋友在实现他们宏大想法的道路上

sentences.en: in getting their big idea off the ground.
sentences.zh: 进展得并不太顺利。

sentences.en: Six months go by.
sentences.zh: 六个月过去了。

sentences.en: It's the day before launch.
sentences.zh: 离上线还有一天。

sentences.en: They still don't have a functioning website.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至还没有一个能正常运行的网站。

sentences.en: The whole business is a website.
sentences.zh: 整个业务就是一个网站。

sentences.en: That's literally all it is.
sentences.zh: 字面意思，这就是全部。

sentences.en: And so I obviously passed on the investment.
sentences.zh: 所以，我显然拒绝了这笔投资。

sentences.en: The name of the company?
sentences.zh: 公司叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Warby Parker.
sentences.zh: 沃比·帕克（Warby Parker）。

sentences.en: They were just named the most innovative company in the world by Fast Company
sentences.zh: 他们刚刚被《快公司》评为全球最具创新力的公司

sentences.en: and they're worth over a billion dollars, which is why my wife handles all our investments now.
sentences.zh: 市值超过了十亿美元，这也是为什么现在我妻子包揽了我们所有的投资。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam and this week on Hidden Brain, Originals, how to spot one, how to be one.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆，本周的《隐藏大脑》原创节目将探讨：如何识别原创者，如何成为原创者。

sentences.en: We bring you my conversation with Adam Grant.
sentences.zh: 我们为您带来我与亚当·格兰特的对话。

sentences.en: He's a professor at the Wharton School at the
sentences.zh: 他是宾夕法尼亚大学沃顿商学院的教授

sentences.en: University of Pennsylvania and he's the author of the new book, Originals, how non-conformists move
sentences.zh: 同时也是新书《原创者：非同凡响的人如何改变世界》的作者。

sentences.en: the world.
sentences.zh: 世界。

sentences.en: I asked Adam what the Warby Parker episode had taught him about the qualities of innovators.
sentences.zh: 我问亚当，沃比·帕克的经历让他对创新者的特质有了什么认识。

sentences.en: They often procrastinate and that's how they incubate ideas.
sentences.zh: 他们经常拖延，而这正是他们孕育点子的方式。

sentences.en: What parents can do to nurture originality in their kids.
sentences.zh: 父母可以做些什么来培养孩子们的独创性。

sentences.en: Their parents focus more on values than rules.
sentences.zh: 他们的父母更看重价值观而不是规则。

sentences.en: And the downside of marching to the beat of your own drum.
sentences.zh: 以及特立独行的负面影响。

sentences.en: One of the risks is, you know, you have everybody marching in a different direction.
sentences.zh: 风险之一就是，你知道的，每个人都在朝着不同的方向行进。

sentences.en: Looking back now, Adam, looking back, if you could go back and talk to the old Adam,
sentences.zh: 现在回想起来，亚当，回顾过去，如果你能回到过去和过去的亚当谈谈

sentences.en: what would you tell that Adam?
sentences.zh: 你会对那个亚当说些什么？

sentences.en: I would say that I was totally wrong about what it takes to be original.
sentences.zh: 我会说，我对成为原创者所需要的条件完全搞错了。

sentences.en: I think of original people as the non-conformists who drive creativity and change in the world.
sentences.zh: 我曾认为原创者就是那些推动世界创造力和变革的非同凡响之人。

sentences.en: And I would say they often procrastinate and that's how they incubate ideas.
sentences.zh: 而我会说，他们经常拖延，这就是他们孕育点子的方式。

sentences.en: They feel the same fears and doubts that the rest of us do.
sentences.zh: 他们感受到的恐惧和怀疑和我们其他人一样。

sentences.en: They just manage them differently.
sentences.zh: 只是他们处理这些情绪的方式不同。

sentences.en: They hate taking risks and they have lots of bad ideas and that's how they get to the good ones.
sentences.zh: 他们讨厌冒险，他们有很多糟糕的点子，而这就是他们找到好点子的途径。

sentences.en: I have to say, though, it's possible that when someone sits on an idea for six months and
sentences.zh: 不过我得说，当一个人把一个点子搁置了六个月

sentences.en: they're an online company and they don't have a website ready to go the day before launch,
sentences.zh: 而他们是一家网络公司，在上线前一天还没准备好网站

sentences.en: it is also possible that they could turn out to be a gigantic failure.
sentences.zh: 也有可能他们最终会成为一个巨大的失败者。

sentences.en: You're just trying to make me feel better about my decision, right?
sentences.zh: 你只是想让我对自己的决定感觉好一点，对吧？

sentences.en: Would you have invested?
sentences.zh: 你会投资吗？

sentences.en: I would not.
sentences.zh: 我不会。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, of course, it's possible that they would fail.
sentences.zh: 对，我的意思是，当然，他们是有可能失败的。

sentences.en: But what I should have paid attention to is they also met all these other characteristics
sentences.zh: 但我当时应该注意的是，他们也符合其他所有特征

sentences.en: that originals tend to bring to the table.
sentences.zh: 这些特征往往是原创者所具备的。

sentences.en: So a lot of times you see that originals are not the people with the deepest expertise.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候你会发现，原创者往往不是那些拥有最深厚专业知识的人。

sentences.en: They're the people with the broadest experience.
sentences.zh: 他们是拥有最广阔经验的人。

sentences.en: And what was so great about Neil's background is he had been selling glasses in the developing world
sentences.zh: 尼尔的背景最棒的地方在于，他一直在发展中国家销售眼镜

sentences.en: and also giving them away to try to help people who couldn't see get their lives in a place
sentences.zh: 还把它们免费送给那些视力不好的人，试图帮助他们过上能够工作的生活

sentences.en: where they could work.
sentences.zh: 能够自食其力。

sentences.en: And he had all sorts of exposure to the fact that you can make glasses a lot more cheaply
sentences.zh: 他接触到各种各样的事实，证明眼镜的制造成本可以比西方世界的垄断企业低得多。

sentences.en: than the monopolies here in the Western world were doing it.
sentences.zh: 西方世界的垄断企业当时的造价远非如此。

sentences.en: They were also really good at questioning the status quo.
sentences.zh: 他们还非常擅长对现状提出质疑。

sentences.en: And this is a hallmark of being an original.
sentences.zh: 这是成为原创者的一个标志。

sentences.en: A lot of people would just say, you know, glasses cost what they coSt.
sentences.zh: 很多人会说，你知道的，眼镜该多少钱就多少钱。

sentences.en: You know, your doctor prescribes them and that's the end of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，医生给你开什么处方就是什么，事情就这么定了。

sentences.en: And they had 60 years of combined experience wearing glasses.
sentences.zh: 他们加起来有60年的戴眼镜经验。

sentences.en: But suddenly one day, one of the founders, Dave, said, why do they cost so much?
sentences.zh: 但突然有一天，其中一位创始人戴夫说，为什么它们这么贵？

sentences.en: Like they've been around for 800 years and they're still more than an iPhone?
sentences.zh: 就像它们已经存在了800年，为什么还比一部iPhone贵？

sentences.en: That doesn't make sense.
sentences.zh: 这说不通。

sentences.en: And once they did research into it, they found out that they could do a lot to lower the price.
sentences.zh: 一旦他们对此进行了研究，他们发现他们可以做很多事情来降低价格。

sentences.en: And I think that was a sign that they were going to take off.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个他们将要腾飞的信号。

sentences.en: In your book, you find that the writer and poet T.S.
sentences.zh: 在你的书中，你发现作家兼诗人T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot, Google's co-founder Larry Page,
sentences.zh: 艾略特、谷歌联合创始人拉里·佩奇

sentences.en: all have something in common.
sentences.zh: 都有一些共同点。

sentences.en: When they have an opportunity to dive headfirst into something, take a big risk,
sentences.zh: 当他们有机会一头扎进某件事、冒巨大风险时

sentences.en: they actually hedge their bets and hesitate.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是在对冲风险并犹豫不决。

sentences.en: So can you talk a little bit about that?
sentences.zh: 所以你能稍微谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Because that runs counter to the way we think that people who are true originals actually behave.
sentences.zh: 因为这与我们认为真正的原创者实际表现出的方式背道而驰。

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: I think what happens is they are afraid of failing, just like you and I might be.
sentences.zh: 我想发生这种情况是因为他们害怕失败，就像你我一样。

sentences.en: And at first, when they have a new idea, they're not sure if it's going to succeed.
sentences.zh: 起初，当他们有一个新点子时，他们并不确定它是否会成功。

sentences.en: They have no idea whether they can support a livelihood based on it.
sentences.zh: 他们完全不知道能否靠它维持生计。

sentences.en: So T.S.
sentences.zh: 所以T.S.

sentences.en: Eliot, you know, poetry is not the most lucrative career.
sentences.zh: 艾略特，你知道的，写诗并不是最赚钱的职业。

sentences.en: He works as a bank clerk to cover his bills and give himself the freedom to do something original as a poet.
sentences.zh: 他靠做银行职员来支付账单，并给自己作为诗人做出原创作品的自由。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think Larry Page and Sergey were both in the position of saying,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，我认为拉里·佩奇和谢尔盖当时都处于这样一种境地

sentences.en: look, what we want to do is we have lots of great ideas.
sentences.zh: 听着，我们想做的是我们有很多伟大的点子。

sentences.en: They were PhD students at Stanford at the time they came up with the idea for Google.
sentences.zh: 他们想出谷歌这个点子时，是斯坦福大学的博士生。

sentences.en: They were.
sentences.zh: 他们确实是。

sentences.en: And, you know, they thought search was bad.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，他们觉得当时的搜索很糟糕。

sentences.en: And they wrote an algorithm to do it better based on, you know, sort of pages linking to other pages being an indication that a page was popular.
sentences.zh: 他们编写了一种算法来更好地完成这项工作，依据的是，你知道的，页面链接到其他页面表明该页面很受欢迎。

sentences.en: And they didn't see that as a career.
sentences.zh: 他们并没有把这看作是一项事业。

sentences.en: They just, you know, kind of said, I know a better way to do this.
sentences.zh: 他们只是，你知道的，说，我知道一个更好的方法来做这件事。

sentences.en: And they built it.
sentences.zh: 然后他们把它建成了。

sentences.en: And they weren't ready to make the leap.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还没有准备好迈出这一步。

sentences.en: They had visions of, you know, continuing to just create knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们怀揣着愿景，你知道的，继续创造知识。

sentences.en: And finish their PhDs as doubtless their parents would have wanted them to do.
sentences.zh: 并完成他们的博士学位，毫无疑问他们的父母也会希望他们这样做。

sentences.en: Yeah, maybe still want them to do.
sentences.zh: 对，也许现在还希望他们这么做。

sentences.en: The great advantage of waiting to make that leap is you don't feel the pressure to rush it to market.
sentences.zh: 等待迈出这一大步的巨大优势在于，你不会感到必须急于将其推向市场的压力。

sentences.en: If they were depending on this for their livelihood, they would have said, we need to get this search engine out there.
sentences.zh: 如果他们靠这个谋生，他们就会说，我们需要把这个搜索引擎推向市场。

sentences.en: We need to get it there now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在就需要把它推出去。

sentences.en: And because they weren't doing that, it was much easier to say, you know, let's get this right.
sentences.zh: 正因为他们没有这么做，所以更容易说，你知道的，让我们把这事做好。

sentences.en: And again, I mean, when you look at what people are doing in basements and in garages, this is what countless people do.
sentences.zh: 再者，我的意思是，当你看看人们在地下室和车库里做的事情，无数人都是这么做的。

sentences.en: I mean, they have a day job.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们有一份正职工作。

sentences.en: They're working as an accountant.
sentences.zh: 他们做着会计的工作。

sentences.en: But they're playing in their garage or their basement and trying to build something new.
sentences.zh: 但他们在车库或地下室里玩弄点子，试图建立一些新的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, it worked out okay for Phil Knight.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对菲尔·奈特来说结果还不错。

sentences.en: He sold shoes out of the trunk of his car for seven years working a day job as an accountant before he finally started Nike.
sentences.zh: 他在正式创立耐克之前，一边做着会计的正职工作，一边在汽车后备箱里卖了七年鞋。

sentences.en: And he learned a lot in those seven years that increased his chances to succeed.
sentences.zh: 他在那七年里学到了很多东西，增加了成功的机会。

sentences.en: So what makes the switch between the point at which you're sort of saying I'm still tinkering versus I'm actually going?
sentences.zh: 那么，是什么让你从那种“我还在小修小补”的阶段转变为“我要大干一场”的呢？

sentences.en: What happens to the people now who just procrastinate and think and plan and endlessly work in their garages and the people who say,
sentences.zh: 那些只知道拖延、思考、规划并在车库里无休止地工作的人，和那些说的人，现在会发生什么？

sentences.en: I'm going to work in my garage for the first two, three, four, five, six years.
sentences.zh: 我要在车库里工作前两、三、四、五、六年。

sentences.en: But eventually I go out and test the waters.
sentences.zh: 但最终我还是会走出去试水。

sentences.en: I think what happens is the fear of failing gets overtaken by the fear of failing to try.
sentences.zh: 我认为发生的事情是，对失败的恐惧被未能尝试的恐惧所取代。

sentences.en: And so, you know, if you have a great search engine or you believe that a film you're making is going to change the world, then at some point you shift from worrying about,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，如果你有一个很棒的搜索引擎，或者你相信你正在制作的电影会改变世界，那么在某个时刻，你会从担心转变为……

sentences.en: you know, regretting making a fool of yourself to regretting never taking a chance.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，后悔自己出丑，变成后悔自己从未抓住机会。

sentences.en: And as you know, that's what psychologists consistently find about regret, that a lot of people are afraid in the moment of taking the risk, but that in the long run,
sentences.zh: 如你所知，心理学家对后悔的研究始终是一致的，很多人在当下害怕冒险，但从长远来看

sentences.en: our biggest regrets are our inactions, the chances we didn't take.
sentences.zh: 我们最大的遗憾是我们的不作为，是我们没有抓住的机会。

sentences.en: And I say, yeah, I might fail, but that's still better than failing to matter.
sentences.zh: 我会说，是的，我可能会失败，但这总比无足轻重、毫无建树要好。

sentences.en: One of the things that you find in the book that I found very intriguing is that very often people who launch new ventures or new careers or new social innovations don't actually choose to do it themselves,
sentences.zh: 你在书中发现的一件让我觉得非常着迷的事情是，很多时候，开展新风险投资、新职业或新社会创新的人实际上并不是自己选择这样做的，而是被其他人征召的。

sentences.en: but they are drafted by other people.
sentences.zh: 而是被其他人征召入局的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was so surprised by this.
sentences.zh: 是的，我也对此感到非常惊奇。

sentences.en: Michelangelo got commissioned to paint the Sistine Chapel, and he's looking up at the ceiling thinking, how in the world could I do that?
sentences.zh: 米开朗基罗受委任去画西斯廷教堂，他抬头看着天花板心想，我怎么可能做到这一点？

sentences.en: And he's terrified, so he flees to Florence, and then he sort of gets coaxed back and talked into giving this a shot.
sentences.zh: 他吓坏了，于是逃到佛罗伦萨，然后又被哄了回来，说服自己试一试。

sentences.en: Martin Luther King doesn't want to lead the Civil Rights Revolution.
sentences.zh: 马丁·路德·金并不想领导民权革命。

sentences.en: His first dream is to be a pastor and then a college president, and he shows up at a meeting, and he's been voted unanimously to lead this movement and basically dragged into it.
sentences.zh: 他的最初梦想是成为一名牧师，然后是大学校长，结果他出现在一次会议上，却被全票推选为这场运动的领导者，基本上是被拉进去的。

sentences.en: And so what you find is often people then rising to the occasion when they're sort of placed in this position that's in some ways an unfamiliar position.
sentences.zh: 所以你发现，当人们被置于某种在某些方面有些陌生的职位时，他们往往能不负众望。

sentences.en: It is, and I think this is sometimes what makes them so effective at these leadership roles or at innovating that they've spent months or years stewing on these ideas,
sentences.zh: 确实如此，我认为正是这一点有时让他们在这些领导岗位或创新上如此高效，他们已经花了几个月或几年的时间来琢磨这些点子，

sentences.en: and they've hatched by the time that somebody pulls them into the spotlight.
sentences.zh: 当有人把他们拉进聚光灯下时，这些点子已经孵化成熟了。

sentences.en: And that leads to the question, when you have an organization and you want to try and get the best talent,
sentences.zh: 这就引发了一个问题，当你拥有一个组织并希望招揽最优秀的人才时，

sentences.en: maybe the thing to do is not sort of to put a job ad out and say who applies for it, but actually to be drafting people who might not on the surface seem like the ideal fit.
sentences.zh: 也许应该做的事情不是发布招聘广告然后看谁来申请，而是实际去征召那些表面上看起来可能并不那么完美契合的人。

sentences.en: I think there's something to be said for that, that originality is brewing in all sorts of unexpected places.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种说法很有道理，独创性正在各种意想不到的地方酝酿。

sentences.en: And so often, as leaders, what we do is we stifle that as opposed to trying to unleash it.
sentences.zh: 而很多时候，作为领导者，我们做的是压制这种独创性，而不是试图释放它。

sentences.en: And there's a lot that can be done to try to figure out, okay, who are the people that are in a position to bring really new ideas into this organization,
sentences.zh: 有很多事情可以做，以弄清楚，好吧，谁是那些有能力将真正的新点子带到这个组织中的人，

sentences.en: and why aren't we hearing from them?
sentences.zh: 以及为什么我们没有听到他们的声音？

sentences.en: And Susan Cain, the quiet author, is fond of saying that there's zero correlation between who's the best talker and who has the best ideas.
sentences.zh: 安静型作家苏珊·凯恩喜欢说，谁最会说话和谁有最好的点子之间没有任何相关性。

sentences.en: And that's a widely supported empirical finding.
sentences.zh: 这是一个得到了广泛支持的实证发现。

sentences.en: And I'd love to do a better job identifying that silent minority and giving them the floor.
sentences.zh: 我很乐意更好地识别出这个沉默的少数群体，并让他们有发言权。

sentences.en: You have to ask how this reflects on our political system, Adam, where the ability to speak and win a public debate is often integral to winning public office.
sentences.zh: 你不得不问，这反映了我们的政治体系什么，亚当，在这个体系中，演讲和赢得公开辩论的能力往往是赢得公职不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: Yeah, you know, what I would love to see is a political system that's based more on skill in leading than it is on speaking.
sentences.zh: 是的，你知道，我最希望看到的是一个更多地基于领导能力而不是演讲能力的政治体系。

sentences.en: So what I want to know is what politicians are going to be the most effective decision makers, who's going to come up with the best strategic vision,
sentences.zh: 所以我想知道的是，哪些政治家将是最有效的决策者，谁能提出最好的战略愿景，

sentences.en: who has expertise in handling conflict.
sentences.zh: 谁拥有处理冲突的专业知识。

sentences.en: We don't see that right now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在没有看到这一点。

sentences.en: And I think we also look for people who want to step forward.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们也在寻找那些想要主动站出来的人。

sentences.en: We look for the person who puts up their hand.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找举手的那个人。

sentences.en: We look for the person who says, I'm the most qualified person.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找那个说“我是最合适人选”的人。

sentences.en: And of course, it's nice to hear initiative.
sentences.zh: 当然，听到进取心是件好事。

sentences.en: It's nice to hear drive.
sentences.zh: 听到动力是件好事。

sentences.en: But that might not actually be the best person for the job.
sentences.zh: 但那可能并不是这份工作的最佳人选。

sentences.en: Yeah, the people that I'm most excited to vote for are the ones who have no interest in the job whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 是的，我最想投票支持的人，恰恰是对这份工作毫无兴趣的人。

sentences.en: I don't know how we get them on the stage.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们怎么能把他们推上舞台。

sentences.en: Right, because of course, having the most compelling speech doesn't necessarily qualify you to know what to do when there's a civil war.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为当然，拥有最引人注目的演讲并不能自然而然地赋予你知道在发生内战时该怎么做的资格。

sentences.en: I want to vote for the candidate who is willing to contradict him or herself, right, and admit to being wrong.
sentences.zh: 我想投票给那个愿意反驳自己、并承认自己错了的候选人，对吧？

sentences.en: Because, you know, some people call that flip-flopping.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，有些人把这叫作摇摆不定。

sentences.en: I think of it as enlightenment.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这叫开悟。

sentences.en: I mean, of the people in your book whom you look at, how many of them have that kind of evolution, if you will,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在你书中提到的那些人物里，有多少人有过这种演变，如果你愿意这么说的话，

sentences.en: where they sort of try something, it doesn't work, they try something else, it doesn't work,
sentences.zh: 也就是他们尝试了某种方法，行不通，又换一种方法，还是行不通，

sentences.en: and they're not actually rigid in their thinking, but they're actually open to being adaptable.
sentences.zh: 而他们的思想其实并不死板，反而是能够顺应变化的。

sentences.en: I think that's one of the hallmarks of being original, is being flexible enough in your thinking to admit,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是富有独创性的标志之一，也就是在思想上足够灵活，能够承认，

sentences.en: you know, this was wrong or this was a bad idea, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这做错了或者这主意很烂，对吧？

sentences.en: Abraham Lincoln, when he came into the presidency, he was initially not going to abolish slavery.
sentences.zh: 亚伯拉罕·林肯刚当上总统时，最初并没有打算废除奴隶制。

sentences.en: He was afraid that it would destroy the union.
sentences.zh: 他担心这会毁了联邦。

sentences.en: And he agonized for six months over that decision before he finally signed the Emancipation Proclamation.
sentences.zh: 他为这个决定痛苦煎熬了六个月，最后才签署了《解放宣言》。

sentences.en: He's a flip-flopper, right?
sentences.zh: 他是个反复无常的人，对吧？

sentences.en: That's one of the most important acts in the history of this country.
sentences.zh: 这是这个国家历史上最重要的法案之一。

sentences.en: Lots of failed inventions while he was trying to pioneer the light bulb.
sentences.zh: 在他努力开创电灯泡的过程中，有过许多失败的发明。

sentences.en: He invented a talking doll so creepy that it scared not only kids, but adults too.
sentences.zh: 他发明了一个会说话的娃娃，诡异得不仅吓坏了小孩子，连大人也吓到了。

sentences.en: A talking doll?
sentences.zh: 一个会说话的娃娃？

sentences.en: A talking doll.
sentences.zh: 一个会说话的娃娃。

sentences.en: I've had nightmares looking at the picture of this.
sentences.zh: 我光是看它的照片就做噩梦了。

sentences.en: So it actually moved its mouth and words came out?
sentences.zh: 所以它真的会动嘴巴而且能发出声音？

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, this was very early, sort of pre-robot.
sentences.zh: 对，这是很早期的产品，可以说是史前机器人阶段。

sentences.en: But he tried to, you know, mine, he tried to mine iron with magnets.
sentences.zh: 但他尝试过，你知道的，采矿，他试图用磁铁开采铁矿。

sentences.en: He tried to preserve fruit with failing techniques.
sentences.zh: 他试图用当时的笨拙技术来保存水果。

sentences.en: And he had to be willing to admit that these ideas were not working out to move on to the ones that did.
sentences.zh: 他必须甘愿承认这些想法行不通，才能继续去追求那些行得通的想法。

sentences.en: But one of the things that this implies is that what distinguishes the great from the ordinary is not necessarily that the great only have great ideas,
sentences.zh: 但这暗示了一点：伟大与平庸的区别，不一定在于伟大的人只有伟大的点子，

sentences.en: but that the great simply have many more ideas than the ordinary.
sentences.zh: 而在于伟大的人拥有的点子比平庸的人多得多。

sentences.en: I think that's exactly the story, right?
sentences.zh: 我觉得事实正是如此，对吧？

sentences.en: The greatest originals are the people who failed the most because they're the ones who tried the moSt.
sentences.zh: 最伟大的独创者往往是失败最多的人，因为他们尝试得最多。

sentences.en: If you study this across lots of different domains, it's not that originals have higher hit rates than their peers.
sentences.zh: 如果你在许多不同的领域研究这一点，就会发现独创者的成功率并不比同行高。

sentences.en: It's just they generate more volume, which gives them more variety and a better shot at something new.
sentences.zh: 只是他们的产量更大，这让他们有了更多样化的尝试，也更有可能碰撞出新鲜事物。

sentences.en: So Bach, Beethoven, Mozart, they were not on average in a typical composition better than their peers,
sentences.zh: 所以巴赫、贝多芬、莫扎特，他们平均水平下的单首作品并不比同行更出色，

sentences.en: but they generated over 600 each, in some cases over a thousand different compositions.
sentences.zh: 但他们每人创作了超过六百首，有时甚至超过一千首不同的作品。

sentences.en: And a few of those were true masterpieces.
sentences.zh: 而其中有那么几首是真正的杰作。

sentences.en: When you looked at the works of Shakespeare, you also found that at the very same time Shakespeare was writing some of his greatest masterpieces,
sentences.zh: 当你审视莎士比亚的作品时，你也会发现，就在莎士比亚创作某些最伟大杰作的同一时期，

sentences.en: he was also writing some of his greatest duds.
sentences.zh: 他也写出了他最糟糕的一些烂作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Have you heard of the Merry Wives of Windsor?
sentences.zh: 你听说过《温莎的风流娘们》吗？

sentences.en: What about the Timon of Athens?
sentences.zh: 还有《雅典的泰门》呢？

sentences.en: If Shakespeare were here today, he'd want us to know that around that time, he also wrote Hamlet and Macbeth.
sentences.zh: 如果莎士比亚今天在这里，他会想让我们知道，大约在那个时期，他还写了《哈姆雷特》和《麦克白》。

sentences.en: So what explains this?
sentences.zh: 那么该如何解释这一点呢？

sentences.en: When the same person is sitting down and writing plays or the same person is sitting down and doing inventions,
sentences.zh: 当同一个人坐下来写剧本，或者同一个人坐下来搞发明时，

sentences.en: how is it they're producing genius and crap at the same time?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们能同时产出天才之作和垃圾？

sentences.en: One, because a lot of us fall in love with our first ideas, and those are the most conventional.
sentences.zh: 第一，因为我们很多人都会爱上自己的第一个点子，而那些通常是最常规的。

sentences.en: Often you have to weed out the familiar in order to get to the unusual, but a lot of people never get to those later ideas.
sentences.zh: 通常你必须剔除那些熟悉的东西才能触及不寻常的事物，但很多人从未走到后面的那些点子。

sentences.en: The second thing is it's just really hard to judge our own ideas.
sentences.zh: 第二点是，评判我们自己的点子实在太难了。

sentences.en: Most of us are way too positive on the ideas we come up with.
sentences.zh: 我们大多数人对自己想出来的点子都过于自信了。

sentences.en: And oftentimes they need to put a bunch of ideas out in the world to get feedback and find out what actually made sense.
sentences.zh: 通常他们需要把一堆点子抛向世界去获取反馈，才能弄清楚什么才真正说得通。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if the same thing is true of Shakespeare.
sentences.zh: 我在想莎士比亚是不是也是这样。

sentences.en: If we actually sat Shakespeare down the year after he wrote the Merry Wives of Windsor and Macbeth,
sentences.zh: 如果我们真的让莎士比亚坐在他写完《温莎的风流娘们》和《麦克白》的第二年，

sentences.en: is it possible that he might have told us, you know, Macbeth, it's okay, but the Merry Wives of Windsor, that's the masterpiece.
sentences.zh: 他有没有可能会告诉我们，你知道的，麦克白还行，但《温莎的风流娘们》那才是杰作。

sentences.en: You know, this is so common among originals.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这在富有独创性的人当中太常见了。

sentences.en: I can't tell you what Shakespeare would have said, obviously,
sentences.zh: 我当然说不出莎士比亚会怎么评价，

sentences.en: because he didn't answer my interviewer requeSt.
sentences.zh: 因为他没有回复我的采访请求。

sentences.en: But, you know, you see this with scientists all the time, that frequently their least cited works are the ones that they think are the greateSt.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道的，你随时都能在科学家身上看到这一点，他们引用率最低的作品往往是他们自己认为最伟大的。

sentences.en: And Beethoven.
sentences.zh: 还有贝多芬。

sentences.en: Beethoven was known as a great self-critic, and yet he was pretty far off the mark in predicting
sentences.zh: 贝多芬以出色的自我批判著称，然而他在预测

sentences.en: which of his pieces were going to be his biggest hits and his biggest flops.
sentences.zh: 自己的哪几首作品会成为最卖座的爆款和最惨淡的滑铁卢时，却差得很远。

sentences.en: My guest today is Adam Grant.
sentences.zh: 我今天的嘉宾是亚当·格兰特。

sentences.en: He's a professor at the Wharton School.
sentences.zh: 他是沃顿商学院的教授。

sentences.en: Coming up, we talk about who gets the chance to be original and how parents can foster this quality in their kids.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我们将讨论谁有机会变得具有独创性，以及父母如何在孩子身上培养这种品质。

sentences.en: I want to look a little bit at perhaps what might be called the dark side of originality,
sentences.zh: 我想探讨一下所谓的独创性的阴暗面，

sentences.en: or maybe the dark side is not the right word.
sentences.zh: 或者说“阴暗面”这个词可能不太准确。

sentences.en: It's more that the benefits of originality are not distributed equally in our society.
sentences.zh: 更确切地说，是独创性带来的好处在我们的社会中并没有得到平等的分配。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think this is a great tragedy that we see both women and racial minority groups being less likely to speak up when they have original ideas.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一个巨大的悲剧，我们看到无论是女性还是少数族裔群体，在有了独创的想法时，都不太敢大声说出来。

sentences.en: Sheryl Sandberg and I wrote an op-ed about this last year called Speaking While Female,
sentences.zh: 谢丽尔·桑德伯格和我去年曾就此联合发表了一篇专栏文章，题为《女性发声》

sentences.en: and we covered a bunch of evidence, including some studies that I ran,
sentences.zh: 我们在文中列举了大量证据，包括我做过的一些研究，

sentences.en: showing that when men spoke up, they were rewarded for it.
sentences.zh: 表明当男性大声说出来时，他们会因此得到奖励。

sentences.en: And when women spoke up, either they were barely heard, and usually some dude sort of wanders in and steals credit for their idea,
sentences.zh: 而当女性发声时，要么根本没人听见，通常还会冒出个大老爷们儿半路截胡、窃取她们的创意，

sentences.en: or they were judged as too aggressive and violating these communal caring stereotypes we have of women.
sentences.zh: 要么她们就会被评判为过于强势，违背了我们对女性那种乐于助人、充满关爱的刻板印象。

sentences.en: And I think those stereotypes lead a lot of women to hold back because they're afraid of backlash.
sentences.zh: 我认为这些刻板印象导致许多女性选择隐忍，因为她们害怕遭到反弹。

sentences.en: And I think that we need many more organizations and I think people in the world to check their biases
sentences.zh: 我认为我们需要更多的组织，也需要世人去审视自身的偏见，

sentences.en: and be receptive to both women and minority groups bringing their ideas to the table.
sentences.zh: 并乐于接受女性和少数族裔群体提出的新想法。

sentences.en: But you have to wonder how many great ideas are not being put on the table at all
sentences.zh: 但你不禁会想，到底有多少绝妙的点子根本没有被提出来，

sentences.en: because people feel hesitant to talk about them.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为人们对谈论它们感到犹豫。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we're missing out on the majority of the original ideas in the world,
sentences.zh: 是的，我觉得我们错失了世界上绝大多数富有独创性的点子，

sentences.en: not because people aren't creative, but because there's a gap between the ideas you have and the ones that you share.
sentences.zh: 不是因为人们缺乏创造力，而是因为你脑海中的点子和你分享出来的点子之间存在着一道鸿沟。

sentences.en: And if you go back to this idea about the volume of ideas, sort of creativity relationship that we talked about earlier,
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下我们之前讨论过的关于点子数量与创造力的关系，

sentences.en: you know, history is obviously full of examples of men doing the majority of the original work in certain fields.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，历史显然充满了男性在某些领域完成大部分原创工作的例子。

sentences.en: And that's largely because they had the freedom to work on lots of ideas,
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是因为他们有自由去研究各种各样的点子，

sentences.en: whereas women were primarily, you know, working on child care and they had a hard time getting their ideas heard.
sentences.zh: 而女性主要精力都在照顾孩子，很难让自己的想法被听到。

sentences.en: In the book, you talk about the idea that birth order, whether you have older siblings or younger siblings,
sentences.zh: 你在书中谈到了出生顺序这一概念，即你是有哥哥姐姐还是有弟弟妹妹，

sentences.en: might play a role in your willingness to take chances.
sentences.zh: 可能会对你冒风险的意愿起到一定作用。

sentences.en: Can you talk about that work?
sentences.zh: 你能谈谈这项研究吗？

sentences.en: This is wildly controversial.
sentences.zh: 这极具争议。

sentences.en: I don't think I've ever seen another realm of social science with more competing results.
sentences.zh: 我想我从未见过社会科学的哪个领域存在如此多针锋相对的研究结果。

sentences.en: But there are a series of studies suggesting that firstborns tend to be slightly more conventional achievers,
sentences.zh: 但有一系列研究表明，长子或长女往往会稍微偏向常规成就的取得，

sentences.en: whereas laterborns are more inclined to challenge the status quo and do things that are a little bit original.
sentences.zh: 而弟弟妹妹们则更倾向于挑战现状，做一些略具独创性的事。

sentences.en: And get this, so you look at over 300 pairs of brothers who played professional baseball,
sentences.zh: 你听这个，如果你观察300多对打职业棒球的兄弟，

sentences.en: and that way you get to do the test within families,
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，你就能在同一个家庭内部进行测试，

sentences.en: and you see that younger brothers are more than 10 times more likely to attempt to steal a base than their older siblings.
sentences.zh: 你会发现弟弟们尝试盗垒的可能性是他们哥哥的10倍以上。

sentences.en: So why is that?
sentences.zh: 那这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: I think that one factor, the popular explanation from Frank Zolloway is that it's about niche picking,
sentences.zh: 我认为其中一个因素，也就是弗兰克·苏洛威提出的流行解释是关于寻找利基市场的，

sentences.en: that, you know, it's hard to stand out by being smarter or stronger than your older siblings.
sentences.zh: 也就是，你知道的，要想通过比哥哥姐姐更聪明或更强壮来脱颖而出是很困难的。

sentences.en: They have a clear advantage academically and athletically.
sentences.zh: 他们在学业和运动方面有着明显的优势。

sentences.en: So what you do is you look for other ways to stand out, and one of those is to take risks or be creative.
sentences.zh: 所以你只能寻找其他方式来脱颖而出，其中一种方式就是冒险或展现创造力。

sentences.en: I think the other part of the story, though, is that parents tend to give more freedom to their later born children.
sentences.zh: 不过，我认为故事的另一个部分在于，父母往往会给后出生的孩子更多的自由。

sentences.en: What is the way you train people to be original?
sentences.zh: 你究竟该如何训练人们变得具有独创性？

sentences.en: What is the way you encourage originality in a company, in an organization, in a family?
sentences.zh: 你又该如何在一家公司、一个组织、一个家庭中鼓励独创性？

sentences.en: Let's start with the family side of it.
sentences.zh: 让我们从家庭层面开始谈起。

sentences.en: If you study some of America's most original architects and compare them with technically skilled but less creative peers,
sentences.zh: 如果你研究美国一些最具独创性的建筑师，并将他们与技术娴熟但创造力较差的同行进行比较，

sentences.en: one of the things that happened in the families of the creative architects was their parents focused more on values than rules.
sentences.zh: 创造力强的建筑师家庭中发生的一件事是，他们的父母更关注价值观而非规则。

sentences.en: And they would say things like, you know, excellence is important in this family.
sentences.zh: 他们会说这样的话，你知道的，卓越在这个家庭里很重要。

sentences.en: What kind of success do you want to achieve?
sentences.zh: 你想取得什么样的成功？

sentences.en: Or we really care about our actions having an impact on others.
sentences.zh: 或者我们非常关心我们的行为对他人产生的影响。

sentences.en: What sort of mark would you like to make on the world around you?
sentences.zh: 你想在你周围的世界留下什么样的印记？

sentences.en: And when their kids grew up, they had a very clear set of guiding principles.
sentences.zh: 当他们的孩子长大后，他们拥有一套非常清晰的指导原则。

sentences.en: They were willing to stand their ground when other people didn't agree with them.
sentences.zh: 当其他人不同意他们的观点时，他们愿意坚守立场。

sentences.en: And they also thought a lot about not just creative self-expression, but saying, how can I do something that's useful to other people?
sentences.zh: 他们不仅会深入思考富有创造力的自我表达，还会去想：“我怎么才能做一些对别人有用的事情呢？”

sentences.en: But why is it that rules-based behavior doesn't produce the same thing as values-based advice?
sentences.zh: 但是，为什么基于规则的行为产生不了与基于价值观的建议相同的效果呢？

sentences.en: When you focus on rules in a family, a lot of times kids learn to follow them,
sentences.zh: 当你在家庭中专注于规则时，很多时候孩子们学会的只是去遵守它们，

sentences.en: which means accepting the status quo and essentially becoming an excellent sheep.
sentences.zh: 这意味着接受现状，本质上就是变成了一只优秀的绵羊。

sentences.en: And when you go to values, kids actually have to think for themselves.
sentences.zh: 而当你转向价值观时，孩子们实际上必须学会独立思考。

sentences.en: What's, you know, this is funny as a parent, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，作为父母，这挺搞笑的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because I, after reading this research, I'm constantly catching myself every time our kids misbehave saying,
sentences.zh: 因为我在读完这项研究后，每次看到我们的孩子调皮捣蛋时，都会不断地抓住自己说：

sentences.en: new rule, and then realizing, nope, we should be talking about what's the value behind this rule.
sentences.zh: “新规矩来了”，然后才意识到，不对，我们应该谈谈这条规矩背后的价值观是什么。

sentences.en: Give me an example where that's happened recently.
sentences.zh: 给我举个最近发生这种事的例子吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So we're sitting at dinner and, you know, one of our family values is respect.
sentences.zh: 我们在吃晚饭，你知道的，我们的家风之一就是尊重。

sentences.en: So we like for them to not get up from the dinner table before everyone's done eating.
sentences.zh: 所以我们希望他们在所有人都吃完饭之前不要离开餐桌。

sentences.en: And, you know, they start to get up and it's like, no, you must sit in your seat.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，他们开始起身，我们就会说：“不行，你必须坐在座位上。”

sentences.en: And then I start to realize, well, what I need to say is here's why that's important to us, right?
sentences.zh: 接着我开始意识到，其实我该说的是：“为什么这对我们很重要，原因在这里，对吧？”

sentences.en: It's not about having the rule.
sentences.zh: 重点不在于定规矩。

sentences.en: It's about saying, look, the reason we like to all sit in our seats is because we want everybody to share a nice family meal.
sentences.zh: 重点在于告诉他们：听着，我们喜欢大家都坐在座位上的原因，是因为我们希望每个人都能共享一顿美好的家庭晚餐。

sentences.en: And we think that's a great way to have, you know, respect for each other.
sentences.zh: 我们认为这是彼此尊重的绝佳方式。

sentences.en: So I think when you talk about originality and creativity, there's a great hunger in our society to want to raise people,
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，当你谈论独创性和创造力时，我们的社会对培养这样的人有着极大的渴望，

sentences.en: to want to have employees be original and be creative.
sentences.zh: 渴望让员工富有独创性和创造力。

sentences.en: Are there downsides to originality and creativity?
sentences.zh: 那么独创性和创造力有什么负面影响吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然有。

sentences.en: A few years ago, Barry Schwartz and I wrote a paper on the too much of a good thing effect,
sentences.zh: 几年前，巴里·施瓦茨和我合写了一篇关于“物极必反效应”的论文，

sentences.en: where we basically argued that all strengths and virtues are like Goldilocks,
sentences.zh: 我们在文中基本认为，所有的优点和美德就像金发姑娘原则一样，

sentences.en: where you can have too much as well as too little.
sentences.zh: 既可能太多，也可能太少。

sentences.en: And there's no question that with originality that can be true.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，独创性也是如此。

sentences.en: One of the risks is that, you know, you have everybody marching in a different direction.
sentences.zh: 其中一个风险就是，你知道的，每个人都朝着不同的方向前进。

sentences.en: And, you know, pioneers need settlers.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，开拓者需要拓荒者。

sentences.en: Leaders need followers.
sentences.zh: 领袖需要追随者。

sentences.en: If everybody's an original, then, you know, you don't have anyone to help implement your ideas.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都是独创者，那么，你知道的，你就找不到任何人来帮你的忙去落实想法了。

sentences.en: But I think the opposite is a greater risk.
sentences.zh: 但我认为对立面才是更大的风险。

sentences.en: If everybody conforms, then we lose out on great ways to improve the world around us.
sentences.zh: 如果人人都墨守成规，那我们就失去了改善周围世界的绝佳途径。

sentences.en: And I don't want people to conform, which is basically saying I will go along with your idea even though I don't believe in it.
sentences.zh: 我可不希望人们墨守成规，那基本上就等于说：“虽然我不信，但我还是随大流吧。”

sentences.en: I want them to think for themselves and sometimes decide that other people's ideas are worth following.
sentences.zh: 我希望他们能独立思考，有时甚至会认定别人的想法也值得追随。

sentences.en: Adam Grant, thank you so much for joining me on Hidden Brain today.
sentences.zh: 亚当·格兰特，非常感谢你今天来参加我们的《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Such a delight.
sentences.zh: 非常荣幸。

sentences.en: This episode was produced by Cara McGurk-Allison with help from Neil Tivolt.
sentences.zh: 本集节目由卡拉·麦格克-埃利森制作，尼尔·蒂沃特提供协助。

sentences.en: Our team includes Jenny Schmidt, Raina Cohen, Parth Shah, Thomas Liu, Laura Querell, and Aditi Banlamoody.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队成员包括珍妮·施密特、雷娜·科恩、帕思·沙阿、托马斯·刘、劳拉·克雷尔以及阿迪蒂·班拉穆迪。

sentences.en: Our supervising producer is Tara Boyle.
sentences.zh: 我们的总制作人是塔拉·博伊尔。

sentences.en: This week, our unsung hero is Tracy Wall.
sentences.zh: 本周我们的无名英雄是特蕾西·沃尔。

sentences.en: Tracy is a former NPR colleague who worked with several of us here on the Hidden Brain team.
sentences.zh: 特蕾西是前NPR同事，曾与我们《隐藏的大脑》团队的几位成员共事过。

sentences.en: She's been a great supporter of our work, and her enthusiasm for storytelling is truly infectious.
sentences.zh: 她一直是我们工作的坚定支持者，她对讲故事的热情确实具有极强的感染力。

sentences.en: Thanks for being a great friend and colleague, Tracy.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你成为一位出色的朋友和同事，特蕾西。

sentences.en: If you're enjoying our U2.0 series, please share it with friends and family who could benefit from these stories.
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢我们的U2.0系列，请把它分享给能从这些故事中受益的朋友和家人。

sentences.en: Next week, we'll bring you our final episode in the series.
sentences.zh: 下周我们将为你带来该系列的最后一集。

sentences.en: It's about a simple, unflashy tool that we should all use more often.
sentences.zh: 这款工具简单而不张扬，我们本该更经常地使用它。

sentences.en: If those checklists had not been integrated to that level at the start of World War II,
sentences.zh: 如果这些检查单在二战开始时没有被整合到那个程度，

sentences.en: it's reasonable to assume that many hundreds and probably thousands of lives would have been lost due to that.
sentences.zh: 可以合理推测，成百上千甚至数千条生命将会因此而消逝。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔，这里是美国国家公共电台。
